subject: URGENT: CriticalCare AI — chat completions timing out & retry amplification
messages:
From: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@criticalcare.ai>
To: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil_sharma@redwood.com>
Cc: CriticalCare AI Support <ops@criticalcare.ai>
Date: Sun, 20 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Intermittent failures during peak for chat completions

Nikhil —

We're seeing a significant spike in 5xx/429s and a number of our streaming chat sessions are timing out client-side during morning peak (08:30–09:00 PT). The behavior looks like this: user starts a session, tokens stream for a few hundred ms, then the client reports a socket timeout and immediately retries. That retry pattern appears to trigger a wider retry amplification across our fleet — we've gone from ~0.5% error rate to >12% in 15 minutes and throughput has collapsed.

We raised a PagerDuty incident (PD-998234). Can Redwood confirm whether this is an origin-side problem or something in the routing/burst control? We need a mitigation plan now — our ops team is throttling client retries but we still need your guidance on server-side controls (connection keepalive, idle timeout thresholds, rate-limit headers, and any quick config flips you can do).

Attaching a small sample of logs and timestamps. This is production traffic — high priority for us.

— Sanjay
Senior SRE, CriticalCare AI
From: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil_sharma@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@criticalcare.ai>
Date: Sun, 20 Jun 2027 09:25:12 -07:00
Subject: Re: URGENT: CriticalCare AI — chat completions timing out & retry amplification

Thanks for the heads-up, Sanjay — sorry you're seeing this. Marcus, can you get SRE on the signal and confirm whether we've got an upstream 429 surge tied to a degraded instance pool or NLB throttling? Key asks:

- Confirm whether 429s are being emitted by the model-serving tier or an edge rate limiter.
- Share per-region token latency percentiles (P50/P95/P99) for the last 30m.
- Check active connection counts and idle timeout evictions in the streaming proxy.

Short-term mitigation ideas to consider (we can iterate):
- Temporarily increase the streaming idle timeout and extend socket keepalive for the CC AI tenant.
- Activate per-tenant soft concurrency cap so we can shed requests gracefully instead of returning hard 5xx.
- If model backends are overloaded, fail-fast with a compatible smaller model variant for queued requests.

Evelyn/Neha — I'll need you to coordinate messages to the customer (ack + expected ETA). Marcus please paste a short technical summary once you have data. I'm putting this on my radar as an exec-level escalation if we can't stabilize within 1 hour.

— Nikhil
Head of Product Ops, Redwood Inference
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil_sharma@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@criticalcare.ai>
Date: Sun, 20 Jun 2027 09:40:03 -07:00
Subject: Re: URGENT: CriticalCare AI — chat completions timing out & retry amplification

Nikhil / team — initial findings (30m snapshot):

- 429s originate at the edge API gateway (rate-limited buckets), but a subset of 5xx (502/504) correlate with degraded model serving pods in us-west-2 (node pressure and intermittent OOM restarts).
- Connection churn: streaming connection drops spike at the proxy layer when backend latency P95 exceeds ~700ms. Clients that implement immediate retry (without jitter/backoff) drive more concurrent connections and push the proxy into a retry storm.
- We observed a pattern where short-lived retries exceed token-rate budget and trigger a short-lived circuit-breaker which returns 502 for in-flight streams.

Immediate mitigations we've applied (t+25m):
- Increased per-tenant soft concurrency from 200 -> 260 for CriticalCare to reduce edge 429s while we scale pools.
- Adjusted idle stream keepalive from 15s -> 45s for CC AI only (hoping to reduce client-side timeouts).
- Triggered a fast scale-up of model-serving pool (+4 instances) and quarantined 2 nodes with high OOM churn.

Next actions (ordered):
1) Continue scaling model pool to target CPU/GPU headroom and monitor 5xx trend (Marcus + infra).
2) Roll a short-term config to return 429 with Retry-After instead of 502 where rate limiting is the cause (edge) to give clients a clear backoff signal (Marcus).
3) Work with CriticalCare to temporarily enable client exponential backoff and jitter — Evelyn/Neha to coordinate customer communication.
4) Post-incident: add a tenant-level adaptive backpressure knob to prevent retry amplification.

Logs attached: ccai_request_logs_20270620.tar.gz (sample). I'll produce a digest with graphs in 30m.

— Marcus
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
To: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@criticalcare.ai>, Nikhil Sharma <nikhil_sharma@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 20 Jun 2027 10:05:27 -07:00
Subject: Re: URGENT: CriticalCare AI — chat completions timing out & retry amplification

Sanjay — thanks for flagging and for sharing logs. We're on it and have applied a few targeted mitigations that should help immediately (Marcus summarized). Customer-facing note for your ops and product teams:

- Expected short-term impact: reduced hard 5xxs; you may see more 429s with Retry-After while we scale.
- Recommended client changes (temporary): add exponential backoff + randomized jitter for retries; respect Retry-After headers if present; reduce aggressive socket-level reconnects to >500ms.

I'll coordinate a 30-minute post-mortem once we stabilize and a 1:1 with your CTO if they prefer an executive readout. ETA for the next update: 30 minutes.

— Evelyn
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference

Update (t+1h30):

- After scaling + config changes, observed 5xx rate dropped from peak 12% -> 1.8% over the last 20 minutes. P95 latency reduced from ~980ms -> ~420ms.
- We still see a small tail of client-triggered reconnects; putting a tenant-specific adaptive token-bucket in front of the proxy is the next dev task.
- Recommend we schedule a short maintenance window tonight (low-traffic) to apply an improved keepalive + backpressure profile for CC AI and run a controlled load test with them.

I've attached the mitigation playbook (sre_mitigation_playbook_v1.pdf) and a link to the incident graphs. If we don't fully stabilize by EOD we should escalate to a leadership briefing and propose a credit for impacted calls (Nikhil to advise).

— Marcus
